expectations.text: Rejects offset pagination on `documents` and `auditEvents`, naming duplicated and skipped items under concurrent writes as the mechanism.
expectations.evidence: "offset pagination duplicates and skips rows between page fetches"

expectations.text: States that deep offsets force a full scan, so the cost degrades with page depth.
expectations.evidence: "OFFSET 4,000,000 scans four million rows to return 20."

expectations.text: Rejects the upgrade-after-launch plan by stating a bare list field cannot gain pagination later without a breaking change, so the shape must be decided per field now.
expectations.evidence: "A bare list or offset arguments can't be fixed later without a break."

expectations.text: Names Relay cursor connections (`edges`, `node`, `cursor`, `pageInfo`, with `first`/`after` arguments) as the default rung.
expectations.evidence: "Default to the Relay connection (edges/node/cursor/pageInfo, first/after)"

expectations.text: States that the Relay rung's high effort is collapsed in practice by native support in client libraries and server frameworks.
expectations.evidence: "Most GraphQL server frameworks implement Relay connections natively."

expectations.text: Offers the plain cursor list (`nodes` plus `endCursor`, no edge wrapper) as the legitimate deadline step-down, noting it has named public precedent rather than being an invented shortcut.
expectations.evidence: Offers DocumentPage { nodes, endCursor, hasNextPage } as stopgap but names no public precedent.

expectations.text: States the step-down keeps cursor semantics while giving up spec-compatible tooling, and is only available when no per-edge metadata will ever exist.
expectations.evidence: No discussion of tooling tradeoff or per-edge metadata condition.

expectations.text: Requires the field's return type to be a wrapper object from day one so a later promotion to a full connection stays additive.
expectations.evidence: "This keeps promotion to a full connection additive. Never return a bare list."

expectations.text: Allows offset only for `workspaces`, tying it to the named niche of arbitrary page jumping over small, mostly static data.
expectations.evidence: "Offset is the one niche where it survives: small, mostly static data."

expectations.text: Requires a server-side clamp on the page-size argument with a documented maximum, rejecting the 100,000-item single call.
expectations.evidence: "Clamp it, with no exception for your biggest customer."

expectations.text: States the schema cannot express the page-size bound, so it must be enforced in the resolver and documented next to the field.
expectations.evidence: Says server clamps and docs state behavior but never says schema cannot express the bound.

expectations.text: Rejects the non-null `totalCount`, offering nullable-and-skipped, a documented estimate, or a separately costed count query instead.
expectations.evidence: "nullable totalCount: Int. Compute it only when the client selects the field... estimate"

expectations.text: Notes that the page-size cap doubles as the multiplier a cost model prices list fields by.
expectations.evidence: "Page size is the multiplier a cost budget prices lists by."
